title: Type and abstraction boundaries
summary: Check construction, conversion, trait commitments and mutation permissions. Independently synthesized entrypoint concepts focus on enforceable boundaries rather than requiring newtypes or compile-time state machines everywhere.

checks.question: Does the new construction or conversion path allow a value that downstream code assumes has already been validated?
checks.applicability: New constructors, public fields, deserialization, newtypes, and conversion implementations.
valid_counterexamples: Validation deliberately occurs at a later boundary before the value is used.
The type is a raw transport object, not a validated domain object.
evidence_needed: A concrete invalid value and its observable consequence.
not_a_rule: Every scalar does not require a newtype.
A type name alone does not establish an invariant.
Construction-time validation cannot freeze external facts that may change later.

checks.question: Does a conversion silently discard range, units, encoding, or identity information that the receiving boundary needs?
checks.applicability: Numeric casts, text/byte conversion, identifiers, time units, and fallible conversion changes.
valid_counterexamples: A preceding bound check proves the conversion is lossless.
Truncation or saturation is explicitly the required behavior.
evidence_needed: Source and destination ranges and units.
Relevant platform width or encoding assumptions.
Supported input that crosses the boundary condition.
not_a_rule: All uses of as are not defects.
TryFrom is not necessary when losslessness is already guaranteed.

checks.question: Does a changed trait bound or representation unintentionally constrain supported callers or promise thread-safety semantics it does not provide?
checks.applicability: Public generic bounds, sealed or marker traits, PhantomData, trait objects, Send/Sync requirements, and abstraction leaks.
valid_counterexamples: The executor genuinely requires Send futures.
A single-threaded design deliberately uses non-Send state.
A stronger bound is part of an approved API change.
evidence_needed: Public API reachability and whether downstream implementations are supported.
Types excluded by the new bound, or variance and auto-trait effects of a changed marker.
not_a_rule: Send and Sync are different properties.
Web application state is not universally required to be Sync.
PhantomData influences type-system behavior; it performs no runtime validation.

checks.question: Does introducing mutation through a shared reference preserve the invariant when callbacks or nested calls access the same value?
checks.applicability: Replacing exclusive borrows with Cell, RefCell or synchronized interior mutability; widening methods from &mut self to &self.
valid_counterexamples: Cell replacement updates independent local state without lending references.
A RefCell borrow is released before calling code that can reenter.
A mutex deliberately coordinates access even on a currently single-threaded deployment.
evidence_needed: All mutation entrypoints and required multi-field invariants.
Dynamic borrow lifetimes and reentrant call paths.
Thread-sharing requirements and how borrow or lock failure is handled.
not_a_rule: Cell can store non-Copy values; particular methods such as get require Copy.
Copy does not imply an equivalent atomic type exists.
Using try_borrow is not a fix unless failure has a valid application meaning.
